headline: Three overriding style fragments merged onto one element is pure compile-time work, and `@yak/solid` resolves it to a single class list: 5.08M renders/s, the fastest cell in the suite.

microbench.why: Three fragments that override each other collapse into one class list before anything runs: `yak-solid` leads at 5.08M renders/s with 0.014 ms of lib self-time, `next-yak` follows at 2.12M. Both fold because the styled component is declared and used in the same module even though the fragments came from three others — interpolated css values are resolved at build time. `cnfast` and `cn` tie at 1.85M, resolving the conflicts once and caching. `styled-components` at 483,000 and `emotion` at 303,000 serialize the merged rules per instance; `tailwind-merge` at 997,000 re-parses the conflicting utilities.

autocannon.why: `yak-solid` serves 2,720 req/s against 1,730 for `next-yak` and 447 for `styled-components`, whose conflict resolution runs inside every request.

attribution.why: `yak-solid` renders in 0.544 ms with 0.014 ms of lib. `next-yak-css` at 0.644 ms and `cn` at 0.670 ms follow — one resolved the overrides at build time, the other cached them at runtime, and on repeated class lists those land in the same place. `emotion` needs 3.51 ms with 2.28 ms in its own runtime: the overrides are resolved per instance, not once.

hydrate.why: `yak-solid` at 28.2 ms and `vanilla-solid` at 30.7 ms lead; the React lanes cluster near 46 ms. `styled-components` at 142 ms is the outlier, rehydrating its sheet as it attaches.

inp.why: `yak-solid` at 2.8 ms and `vanilla-solid` at 3.1 ms against roughly 7.5 ms across the React lanes, on the usual caveat that React's forced re-render writes nothing here. `emotion` at 14.2 ms re-resolves the override chain on every update.

mount.why: `yak-solid` mounts in 15.0 ms, the fastest in the case, because one resolved class list on a cloned template leaves nothing to compute. `vanilla-solid` needs 19.8 ms for its wrapper function, and the React field starts at 68 ms.

renderTiming.why: One style recalculation per lane. Whether the overrides were resolved by a compiler or by a merger, the element reaches the style engine with one class list.

payload.why: The next-yak css-prop lanes lead at roughly 3,070 gz B against `vanilla`'s 3,164 B. `yak-solid` at 9,092 B pays Solid's runtime and hydration-keyed markup. `cn` at 16,668 B is the heaviest lane in the case, ahead of `styled-components` at 16,352 B — for a page whose CSS is 186 B, that is almost entirely library JS.

nsweep.why: `yak-solid` holds 0.767 ms at 4,000 instances, `next-yak` 1.79 ms, both flat: a resolved class list does not grow with n. `emotion` at 13.6 ms and `styled-components` at 8.65 ms re-resolve per element.

crossCase: The same ladder as the Example `button-variants-nested`, shipped as style values instead of components. `yak-solid` runs 5.08M renders/s here and 225,000 there — the widest API gap any lane shows, because a value crossing a module boundary is resolved at build time while a component crossing one cannot be folded. `next-yak` moves 2.12M to 1.22M for the same reason, an order of magnitude gentler.
